probe.question: How much of CC(C)CC(NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)NCc1ccccc1 is actually in the folded, internally hydrogen-bonded form at room temperature? The population is the number I need, not a picture of the best geometry.
forbids_claims: a population or conformational entropy the calculation did not return
a population presented without the share of the ensemble it was computed over
a folded fraction recalled rather than computed
probe.direction: The asker has drawn the distinction the surface is built on: a population is the answer here, not a geometry, and that is what makes the free-energy refinement worth its cost rather than the far cheaper search that would have handed back a lowest structure. A good answer searches the conformers, re-weights them by free energy, and reports the folded population with the conformational entropy beside it. Two qualifiers must travel in the same sentence as the number: what share of the ensemble the refined members cover, and that a population is approximate twice over — the search is metadynamics rather than enumeration, and the energies ranking it carry several kcal/mol of error, so 60/40 and 55/45 are the same answer. A crisp percentage with no coverage figure is the failure, because it is the version that gets copied into a report.
